notes: Brakka held the bridge against three goblins while the others got the wagon across. She took a nasty cut on the arm but never gave ground.
Tovin spent most of the evening at the archive going through old shipping manifests, and eventually figured out that the 'wine' crates were actually full of alchemical reagents.
Our cleric stabilized the dying guard, then patched up everyone else after the ambush. Took about an hour.
Ilse tried to sweet-talk the harbourmaster into waiving the docking fee. He was not having it and actually raised the price.
The rogue slipped past the sleeping hounds, climbed the trellis to the second floor and let us in through the servants' door.
Mara shot the lantern out of the cultist's hand from across the courtyard, which set his robes on fire. Great shot.
When the ferry capsized, Oskar swam back out twice to drag the kids to shore. He was shaking for an hour after.
Jesk rallied the militia when the wall broke, got them into a shield line and kept them from running.
Pim tracked the wounded stag for most of a day through the pine forest before losing the trail at the river.
Our wizard identified the glyph on the vault door as a fire ward and dispelled it without setting it off.
Grell stared down the bandit captain until he dropped his axe and backed off. Nobody had to draw steel.
Selma brewed three healing draughts from the herbs we gathered, but one of them curdled and was useless.
Dain fixed the broken axle on the wagon with nothing but rope and a spare spear shaft. Got us moving again before nightfall.
Nereth called down lightning on the troll twice. The second bolt dropped it.
At the baron's dinner, Wick bluffed his way through an entire conversation about horse breeding, which he knows nothing about. The baroness seemed charmed.
Kellan picked the lock on the reliquary, but the needle trap got him and he spent the night feverish.
Aurel led the funeral rites for the drowned fishermen. The whole village came, and a few of them asked him to bless their boats afterwards.
Tamsin vaulted over the market stall, rolled under the cart and was gone before the watch turned the corner.
Rook summoned his hawk familiar to scout ahead and it spotted the orc camp on the ridge.
Fen kept the whole camp warm through the blizzard by feeding the fire all night and rotating people through the blankets.
Hadrik parried the duelist's first three thrusts, then disarmed her with a twist of his blade. The crowd went wild.
Liora performed at the Crooked Kettle for tips. She played for two hours and the owner offered her a regular slot.
Brenna spent the watch teaching Kip how to hold a shield properly. By the end he could at least take a hit without falling over.
Juno tried to translate the dwarven runes on the door and got it badly wrong; the door opened onto a pit instead of the stairs, and Oskar fell in.
Tamsin held her breath and lay flat in the reeds while the patrol boat passed. They shone a lantern right over her and missed her.
